key_insight: A large open-source LLM (Llama 3.3 70B) can accurately identify PCI notes and extract many variables needed to classify complex PCI from cath reports.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart abstraction and make large-scale cardiovascular research phenotyping faster and more scalable.
method: Evaluated three open-source LLMs: Llama 3.3 70B, Meditron-7B, and BioMistral-7B.
Used manually annotated cardiac catheterization reports from three hospitals in Yale New Haven Health.
Compared model extraction of PCI status and complex PCI criteria such as stent count, lesion count, CTO, bifurcation PCI, and total stent length.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 1,412 notes (596 PCI procedures); Llama 3.3 70B achieved 100.0% sensitivity for PCI identification and 97.7% sensitivity for complex PCI classification, though specificity and PPV were lower for the complex task.
watch_item: Performance was weaker for variables needing contextual reasoning, so human review may still be needed for ambiguous cases and deployment across new sites.
paper_title: Automated Identification of Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention from Cardiac Catheterization Reports Using Large Language Models
